decision_table.name: Determine_NM_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file New Mexico state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in NM (office, employees, property)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
NM filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in NM if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in NM - Employees working in NM - Tangible personal property located in NM - Real property located in NM
Reference: New Mexico Statutes § 7-4-2 (Nexus standards) Reference: NM Taxation and Revenue Department Publication FYI-350

actions.action: // Economic nexus established per Wayfair - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
NM filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair).
Economic nexus threshold: $100,000 gross receipts in NM.
New Mexico simplified its economic nexus requirements by eliminating the transaction count threshold. Only the gross receipts threshold ($100,000) applies.
Following South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018), NM requires filing if a corporation exceeds economic nexus threshold, even without physical presence.
Measurement: Prior year sales determine nexus (2024 sales determine 2025 nexus).
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: NM Taxation and Revenue Department Economic Nexus Guidance Reference: New Mexico Statutes § 7-9-3.5 (Economic nexus provisions)

No NM nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not meet physical presence or economic nexus thresholds. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: New Mexico Statutes § 7-4-2 (Nexus requirements)

decision_table.name: Calculate_NM_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate NM state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income. Includes adjustments for NM's decoupling from federal bonus depreciation, IRC 168(n), and IRC 163(j) provisions.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
NM state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
NM ADDITIONS to federal taxable income include: - Interest income from U.S. government obligations (exempt federally, taxable to NM) - Bonus depreciation addback - NM decouples from IRC § 168(k) (100% bonus depreciation for qualified property placed in service after 1/19/2025) - IRC § 168(n) qualified production property expensing addback (100% expensing provision - effective for tax years beginning on or after 1/1/2027) - IRC § 163(j) business interest deduction adjustments (NM decouples from federal interest deduction changes) - State income taxes deducted on federal return - Expenses related to exempt income
NM SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income include: - Interest on NM state and municipal bonds - NM net operating loss deduction (subject to NM limitations) - Dividend income eligible for NM dividend received deduction (85%) - Certain refunds of state income taxes
SIGNIFICANT 2025 REFORM: Senate Bill 151 (2025) represents one of the most significant corporate tax reforms of the year. NM decoupled from federal provisions to prevent erosion of the corporate tax base and corporate tax avoidance.
Decoupling provisions: - IRC § 168(k) bonus depreciation: Addback required - IRC § 168(n) qualified property: Addback required (effective 2027) - IRC § 163(j) business interest: Adjustment required
Reference: NM Form CIT-1 Schedule A (Additions to Federal Taxable Income) Reference: NM Form CIT-1 Schedule B (Deductions from Federal Taxable Income) Reference: New Mexico Statutes § 7-2A-8 (Adjustments to federal taxable income) Reference: Senate Bill 151 (2025 corporate tax reform)

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have NM nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_NM_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate NM state corporate income tax. Applies NM 5.9% flat rate to apportioned and adjusted taxable income. NM changed to flat rate system in 2025 (previously had graduated rates).

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
NM state corporate income tax calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to NM: × [NM apportionment percentage] 3. NM additions: + [Federal interest, bonus depreciation, IRC 168(n), IRC 163(j), etc.] 4. NM subtractions: - [NM municipal interest, NM NOL, dividend deductions, etc.] 5. NM taxable income: = [Result] 6. NM tax rate: × 5.9% (FLAT RATE - effective 2025) 7. NM income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. NM credits: - [Job creation, rural area, technology jobs, film, renewable energy, etc.] 9. NM tax liability: = [Final tax]
NM uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% sales factor).
NM tax rate history: - 2025+: 5.9% flat rate (simplified from graduated rates) - Before 2025: Graduated rates (4.8% to 5.9% depending on income level)
The 2025 change to a flat 5.9% rate represents a relatively rare case of a corporate income tax rate INCREASE in recent years, as NM moved from graduated rates (starting at 4.8%) to a flat 5.9% on all income.
NM provides various tax credits including: - Job training incentive program credit - Rural job tax credit - Technology jobs and research and development tax credit - Film production tax credit - Renewable energy production tax credit - Sustainable building tax credit
Reference: NM Form CIT-1 (Corporate Income and Franchise Tax Return) Reference: New Mexico Statutes § 7-2A-5 (Tax rate of 5.9% flat rate - effective 2025) Reference: New Mexico Statutes § 7-4-10 (Single-sales apportionment) Reference: NM Taxation and Revenue Department Corporate Tax Guidance 2025 Reference: Senate Bill 151 (2025 corporate tax reform)

No NM nexus - no tax liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in NM. Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: New Mexico Statutes § 7-4-2 (Nexus requirements)

No NM taxable income - no tax liability.
Corporation has NM nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments. Any estimated payments are refunded.
NM net operating loss (NOL) rules: - NM allows NOL carryforward for 20 years - No carryback allowed (as of 2025) - NOL limited to prevent complete elimination of tax liability
Reference: NM Form CIT-1 (Corporate Income and Franchise Tax Return) Reference: New Mexico Statutes § 7-2A-8 (Net operating loss deduction)
